config.classes_note: Four classes, each the census's own intersection, evidence kind or labor object for the entity, stated by field sources at the loci given: (1) the employment effects of AI (census intersection 'gains-and-losses', evidence kind 'observed employment outcome'; B1 title and abstract, B11, B1-pdf); (2) occupational AI exposure (census labor_object, negative_tags[3]; B1, B11); (3) AI usage that automates against usage that augments (census lv_intersection, the archive's reading; B11, B1); (4) entry-level and early-career employment (census findings, direction; B1, B1-pdf, B11). The archive's instruments of labor direction bear on these classes only where a sentence applies them: the Directionality of Semantic Labor (#771, EA-MPAI-DSL-01: 'Directionality of semantic labor measures where a synthetic system's labor flows relative to the commissioned task'; its laborvector.org definition surface #1392), the DS-6 directionality stack (#771, Semantic Integrity Markers: 'the DS-6 directionality stack') and user labor drag (#771, Semantic Integrity Markers: 'user labor drag'; ULD among the reflexive extensions) measure a synthetic system's labor against a commissioned task, which is the census's intersection 'labor-with-ai' and not this entity's ('gains-and-losses'); they enter the class (3) reading only through the census's lv_intersection, the archive's reading that the automation ratio is a usage measure of who directs the task, and are admitted only where a deposit sentence itself says so. The semantic-labor line (the semantic economy, the semantic proletariat #1545) enters by reading where a sentence applies its category to displacement, exposure or the distribution of gains. Aliases: the dashboard's name, the paper's title with its question mark and its subtitle, and the authors' pair as the paper is cited. The bare phrase 'canaries in the coal mine' is not an alias: it is the idiom, the homonym the composition gives; archive uses of the idiom are read as the homonym's and recorded, never admitted as the entity's. Admission by reading (§3.4): a bare mention, a reference-list entry or a keyword is not a claim.
